timing: Median synchronized wall milliseconds. Two warmup calls precede each operation. First-call times excluded from comparisons.
isolation: Serial GPU processes; no concurrent training/test workload. Decode and training comparisons repeated in reverse order. Long decode has one pair only.
baseline_execution: Current benchmark harnesses, loading the saved baseline runtime module for the selected path. All other components/configuration held fixed. Baseline files match the named Git commit byte-for-byte.
changes: Decode validates each public batch once, then enqueues its rows without repeating whole-model/version/capacity checks per row.
Decode uploads six scheduling-index lists in one tensor transfer and splits device views.
Packed training uses already-sorted sequence IDs directly; removes variable-size boundary extraction and repeat_interleave reconstruction.
interpretation: Short/ragged decode latency decreased about 10-15%; prefill decreased about 5-10%. Long decode changed about 1.5%. Training forward metadata is cheaper, but complete optimizer-step gains are modest/noisy: short 0.5-7.2%, longer 2.0-2.2%. No end-to-end downstream or trained-policy speed claim.
limitations: Synthetic backbones; no tokenizer/environment/data-loader time included.
Compilation/disk caches make first-call times unsuitable for before/after comparison.
Separate-process variability matters for small gains. No confidence interval or broad hardware generalization.
Memory allocation was essentially unchanged; long decode transient peak rounded to 835 vs 836 MiB.
